conventions.convention: N=2^n with n≥0; addresses use big-endian encoding into {0,…,N−1}. The zero-qubit address register is one-dimensional.
Access is the total Boolean coherent XOR oracle. Phase marking uses one bit query with a response in |−⟩; candidate verification is a separate bit query. Controlled-query access is not supplied.
The iterate is G=R_s O_M, with R_s=2|s⟩⟨s|−I. Exact callable H and X and a separately costed exact reflection implementation are required.
The invariant-plane basis is ordered (|B⟩,|G⟩), giving positive-angle rotation by 2θ and initial coordinates (cos θ,sin θ). The normalized good/bad vectors require 0<t<N.
Known-count exact selection maximizes over integer k=0,…,K, K=ceil(sqrt(N/t)), and chooses the least maximizer. The t=0 branch returns none without querying.
Randomized known-count search uses nine fresh rounds. For 0<t≤N/2, a b-bit label outside {0,…,K−1} rejects the entire round without querying; it is not resampled within that round.

BBHT rounds begin at ℓ=1, use M_ℓ=ceil((3/2)^ℓ), first verify a uniform direct sample, then choose j uniformly from {1,…,M_ℓ}. Every round uses fresh randomness and registers; t=0 causes perpetual continuation.
The success law applies to nonnegative integer iteration counts. The t=0 and t=N endpoints are treated directly without normalizing an empty marked or unmarked component.

load_bearing.statement: For 0<t<N, θ=arcsin sqrt(t/N), and integer k≥0, the marked-address probability after k iterates from |s⟩ is p_k=sin²((2k+1)θ). For t=0 it is 0, and for t=N it is 1, for every integer k≥0.
For 0<t<N, G=R_s S_M preserves the marked/unmarked plane and has matrix [[cos(2θ),−sin(2θ)],[sin(2θ),cos(2θ)]] in the ordered basis (|B⟩,|G⟩); the initial column is (cos θ,sin θ).
One execution of alg-qa-11-grover-iterate makes exactly one standard bit-query call through phase kickback. Response preparation and reflection make no oracle calls and are charged separately.
For a=t/N and θ=arcsin sqrt(a), if 0<a≤1/2, some integer 0≤k≤ceil(1/sqrt(a)) has p_k≥1−a. If 1/2<a≤1, k=0 lies in this range and p_0=a>1/2.
For 0<a=t/N<3/4, θ=arcsin sqrt(a), and J uniform on {1,…,M}, every positive integer M≥4/sqrt(a) gives E[sin²((2J+1)θ)]≥3/8.
For 0<t≤N/2, a=t/N, θ=arcsin sqrt(a), K=ceil(1/sqrt(a)), and J uniform on {0,…,K−1}, E[sin²((2J+1)θ)]=1/2−sin(4Kθ)/(4K sin(2θ))≥1/4.

For t>0 and n≥1, the exact rational recurrence through index 2K+1 has O(Kn)-bit numerators and denominators, and schoolbook arithmetic selects the least maximizing k in O(K²n²) classical bit operations. For n=0 the cost is O(1); for t=1 the preprocessing can be exponential in n.

seams_checked.note: The XOR-to-phase conversion uses X then H, one bit query, and an unchanged |−⟩ response. No controlled phase access or free preparation is inferred.
Exact count is declared public input only in known-count procedures. Worst-case query costs and finite-prefix expected costs remain distinct; verification calls are counted.
Big-endian address indexing, ordered product bases, and the one-dimensional empty register are preserved. The measurement calculation sums over the response register.
Dirac bras and outer products agree with the root linear-first pairing; the real plane coordinates introduce no conjugation discrepancy.
The signs R_s=2P_s−I and S_M=I−2Π_M are retained. Reflection implementation is explicitly supplied and costed; controlled access is not assumed.
The exact H and X matrices give the stated uniform and response preparations. Callable-gate access is separately declared.
Chronological order yields R_s O_M. Gate occurrences, reflection operations, measurements, and oracle calls remain separate resource coordinates.
Pure vectors are used on positive-dimensional registers; normalized projectors and terminal probabilities are consistent with the cited state interfaces.
The circuit cost interface is used without inferring uniform polynomial-time generation. Exact maximization is expressly allowed exponential classical preprocessing.

The downstream fixed-one schedule applies the integer recurrence and rounding theorem on singleton inputs, handles empty inputs by verification, and charges one raw query per simulated iterate plus final verification.
